_comment: Per-project SEO site config consumed by seo_site_config.py. Copy to your project root as seo-site-config.json (or point SEO_SITE_CONFIG / --site-config at it). Keys starting with '_' are ignored, so these inline notes are safe to keep or delete. The example below models a generic SaaS site; replace every value with your own taxonomy.
_comment_target_domain: Bare domain used for citation matching (subdomains match too).
_comment_known_locales: Locale path prefixes stripped before cluster matching, so /de/pricing clusters like /pricing.
_comment_clusters: Ordered URL-path rules, first match wins; anything unmatched falls back to 'other'. Put more specific prefixes before general ones (e.g. /blog/category/ before /blog/). Trailing slashes are irrelevant: '/blog/' matches /blog, /blog/ and /blog/x.
_comment_commercial_paths: Path prefixes considered transactional; they cluster as 'commercial' when no cluster rule matched first. '/' matches the homepage only.
_comment_commercial_signals: Lowercase substrings that mark real user intent. Any query containing one of these is NEVER classified as noise, even if a noise pattern matches. Trailing/leading spaces are significant ('best ' avoids matching 'bestseller').
_comment_noise_patterns: Regexes applied to the lowercased query; a match classifies the query as noise (dropped from the focused core, kept in the .raw.csv). Typical noise: raw ID lookups, support/error queries, brand-navigation for other products, scrapy database-style lookups.
_comment_purpose_patterns: Regexes that cancel a noise classification (strongest override, checked before commercial_signals). Use for audience/purpose qualifiers that prove real intent.
_comment_priority_bands: Cluster names feeding the P0-P3 rubric. P0 = commercial heart of the business (needs impressions >= 50 OR position <= 20). P2 = informational authority (needs impressions >= 30). P1 is cluster-independent: impressions >= 100 and position 4-30. Everything else is P3.
